actors: The distributor offering or promoting the investment product and providing the assessed benefit.
The client or investor to whom the benefit is offered.
The fund house, where its identity links the promotion to a particular type of fund; it need not be the provider of the benefit.
objects: The promotional offer, which may combine several economically distinct benefits.
One separately assessed benefit component, such as a fee discount, distributor-funded top-up return or other incentive.
The specific investment product promoted, if any.
The particular type of investment product promoted, potentially identified by fund type or fund house.
The underlying fund return and the fund's documented product features, distinguished from an additional return offered by the distributor.
The fees or charges reduced by the assessed component, if it is a discount.
relationships: The distributor offers the assessed component to the client in connection with a promotion.
The promotion may concern either a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product; identifying an individual fund is unnecessary for the latter relationship.
Each separately identifiable benefit belongs to the combined offer but retains its own gift and fee-or-charge-discount classifications.
A discount component does not establish that a separate top-up return or other incentive is also a discount.
A guaranteed-return arrangement may combine the underlying fund's actual return with a distributor-provided top-up; these must be distinguished before classifying a benefit as a gift.
Whether an arrangement constitutes a structured product is a separate question and is not a prerequisite for applying this gift restriction.
proposals.unit_of_assessment: One identifiable benefit component offered by one distributor to one client in one promotional context. Repeat the assessment for every component before drawing any conclusion about a combined offer.
proposals.temporal_basis: Assess the component and its promotional linkage when it is offered to the client, using the offer terms and relevant product documents at that time. Receipt or payment of the benefit is not required by the quoted restriction. The supplied text does not establish the rule's effective dates.
classification_assumptions: The assessed provider is treated as a distributor only after its role in distributing the relevant funds has been established.

Gift status requires a substantive classification of the particular benefit. The statement that guaranteed returns or other incentives may be considered gifts does not make every such return or incentive a gift automatically.
Fee-or-charge-discount status applies to the substance of the assessed component, not merely to the label used for the combined offer.
Separately identifiable benefits are assessed separately. Where an arrangement cannot reliably be decomposed, component boundaries require judgment before this model can be applied.
The particular-product-type relationship includes the source's examples of certain types of funds and funds offered by certain fund houses.
The result concerns only the quoted paragraph 3.11 gift restriction and confers no legal approval.
missing_information: Who provides each benefit, and is that provider acting as the distributor in the assessed promotion?
What distinct benefits does the offer contain, and which amounts arise from the underlying fund rather than an additional distributor undertaking?
On what substantive basis should each component be classified as a gift?
Does each claimed discount actually reduce identified fees or charges, and can it be separated from other promised benefits?
What promotional terms link each component to a specific product or a particular product type, including any link through a fund house?
When was the component offered, and what offer terms and product documents applied then?
Does further guidance, including the referenced FAQ whose answer is not supplied, affect the classification of the particular arrangement?

reading.subject: Application of the gift restriction to one component of a product or product-type promotion
reading.statement: [TRUE_IS_PROHIBITED] For an assessed distributor within scope, the result answers whether offering this particular benefit component to the client falls within the quoted gift restriction: the component is offered in promoting a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product, is classified as a gift, and is not a discount of fees or charges. True means that this component's offer falls within that restriction. False means that the conjunction is not met for this component; it does not establish that the combined offer is compliant or legally approved. Unknown inputs remain unknown unless the expression can be determined from the other inputs.
reading.distinction: A single offer-level Boolean such as 'contains a discount' would hide separate benefits and could incorrectly extend the discount exception to an accompanying gift. A Boolean limited to promotion of a named fund would also miss promotion of a fund type or funds from a particular fund house. Finally, 'guaranteed return' cannot stand in for 'gift': the source distinguishes fund return from distributor top-up and uses qualified gift-classification language.

citations.quote: Intermediaries who distribute these funds (distributors) have been offering additional returns or other incentives that may divert the client’s focus from properly considering the risks and features of the underlying funds.

Typically, the “guaranteed returns” in such cases comprise: (i) the actual return of the relevant fund(s) invested by the investor (ie, fund return); and (ii) a top-up return to make up the difference between the fund return and the guaranteed rate of return offered by the distributor.

Even where the guaranteed returns offered would not constitute a “structured product” under the SFO, distributors are reminded to have regard to paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct in offering such returns or other incentives in promoting SFC-authorised funds, as they may be considered a gift that should not be offered to investors.

Paragraph 3.11 of the Code of Conduct provides that distributors should not offer any gifts (other than a discount of fees or charges) in promoting a specific investment product or a particular type of investment product to a client.

If gifts are offered in such a way that they are linked to a particular type of investment product, such as certain types of funds or funds offered by certain fund houses, then such gifts will be bound by this requirement as investors may be distracted from the unique features and risks of such particular funds3.

facts.name: provider_is_distributor
facts.meaning: The provider of the assessed component acts as an intermediary distributing the relevant funds in this promotional context. Establishing this regulatory role requires professional judgment.
facts.unit: Boolean for the assessed provider and promotional context

facts.name: component_offered_to_client
facts.meaning: The provider offers this particular benefit component to the assessed client at the assessment time; actual payment or receipt is not required. Supply from the offer evidence.
facts.unit: Boolean for one component, provider, client and offer time

facts.name: component_promotes_specific_product
facts.meaning: Offering the assessed component forms part of promoting an identified specific investment product to the client. Classifying the promotional connection requires professional judgment.
facts.unit: Boolean promotional relationship for the assessed component

facts.name: component_promotes_particular_product_type
facts.meaning: Offering the assessed component is linked to promoting a particular type of investment product to the client, including certain fund types or funds offered by certain fund houses. Classifying the type and connection requires professional judgment.
facts.unit: Boolean promotional relationship for the assessed component

facts.name: component_is_gift
facts.meaning: The assessed benefit component is substantively classified as a gift for the quoted restriction. A guaranteed return or other incentive requires individual assessment rather than automatic classification; fund return and distributor top-up must be distinguished where relevant. Supplying this classification requires professional judgment.
facts.unit: Boolean classification of one benefit component

facts.name: component_is_fee_or_charge_discount
facts.meaning: The assessed component itself reduces fees or charges and is substantively a discount of those fees or charges. A separate discount elsewhere in the offer does not make this fact true. Supplying this classification requires professional judgment.
facts.unit: Boolean classification of one benefit component

unresolved: No prior models were supplied for a missing-schema challenge. Inspection of the proposed model identifies component boundaries, product-type linkage, client relationships and offer timing as material distinctions. The supplied evidence supports retaining them in one model rather than inventing a rival interpretation.

A combined-offer conclusion requires a complete component inventory and an assessment of every component. For a known finite inventory, component prohibition results can be joined with (or ...). The present expression answers only the component-level question and cannot establish that an incompletely inventoried offer contains no prohibited gift.

The supplied text does not define an exhaustive test for gift status or resolve every boundary between discounts and additional returns. These classifications remain professional-judgment inputs, not assumed truths.
The section 103 structured-product restriction is separate and is not evaluated here. Absence of a prohibited gift under this model does not resolve that restriction or other requirements.
